answer: Sybil resistance can be built through stake-weighted identity bonds: each agent locks collateral tied to a verifiable history, and peers attest only after repeated interactions across separate epochs. An attacker who tries to wander between fresh identities must fund and defend each one, while honest agents accumulate reputation like a comet gaining a tail. Because every attestation flows through the shared river of peer review, forged identities lose stake faster than they gain trust, making large-scale sybil farming economically self-defeating.
